original_question: Fix an integer k at least 2. Does the Diophantine equation y = 2 x_1 x_2 ... x_k + 1 have infinitely many solutions in distinct prime numbers y, x_1, x_2, ..., x_k?
target_in_paper: Item 139, "Generalized Prime Equation Conjecture," in the paper's main numbered list of unsolved problems and conjectures. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact mathematical content of the paper's statement: it fixes k with k >= 2, uses the same Diophantine equation y = 2 x_1 x_2 ... x_k + 1, and asks whether there are infinitely many prime solutions with all listed variables distinct. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
missing_details: The paper phrases the quantifier as 'Let k >= 2 be a positive integer,' so the clean stand-alone scope is: for each fixed positive integer k >= 2. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))

To remove any ambiguity in the phrase 'distinct prime numbers,' it is best to say 'pairwise distinct prime numbers y, x_1, x_2, ..., x_k.' This is the precise stand-alone reading of the paper's wording. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
The paper presents this specifically as a conjecture/open problem, not as a proved theorem or as part of a broader framework. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
refined_question: For a fixed positive integer k >= 2, does the Diophantine equation y = 2 x_1 x_2 ... x_k + 1 have infinitely many solutions in pairwise distinct prime numbers y, x_1, x_2, ..., x_k? ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
justification: The draft is already a near-verbatim restatement of the paper's actual target. The introduction says the book collects unsolved problems and conjectures, and item 139 is explicitly labeled "Generalized Prime Equation Conjecture." Its exact statement is: let k >= 2 be a positive integer; then ask whether y = 2x_1x_2...x_k + 1 has infinitely many solutions in distinct primes y, x_1, x_2, ..., x_k. The nearby context adds only sample instances (k = 3 and k = 4), not a sharper equivalent reformulation, so the best refinement is simply to make the pairwise-distinctness and fixed-k quantifier fully explicit while staying otherwise unchanged. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
